entries.summary: EMA published a Q&A clarifying the PIP compliance verification procedure and paediatric reward eligibility.
entries.why_it_matters: Regulatory affairs teams must review the updated verification steps and reward criteria to ensure their submissions comply with EMA expectations.

entries.label: Health Canada
entries.title: Notice of Compliance (NOC) Data Extracts
entries.description: The data extract is a series of compressed ASCII text files of the Notice of Compliance (NOC) database.
entries.summary: The Notice of Compliance (NOC) database is now available as a series of compressed ASCII text files.
entries.why_it_matters: RA teams handling NOC data should adjust their data extraction and analysis workflows to accommodate the new compressed text format.

entries.label: EMA News
entries.title: Clinical trial applications advice pilot becomes permanent
entries.description: The Accelerating Clinical Trials in the EU (ACT EU) advice pilot, which helps sponsors prepare clinical trial applications, will become a permanent initiative from January 2027…
entries.summary: The Accelerating Clinical Trials in the EU (ACT EU) advice pilot will become a permanent initiative from January 2027.
entries.why_it_matters: RA teams sponsoring clinical trials in the EU will now have ongoing access to the ACT EU advice service, so they should plan to utilize it for trial application preparation.

entries.label: Health Canada
entries.title: Product monograph brand safety updates
entries.description: Product monograph brand safety updates for Submissions cleared between 01-09-2026 and 30-09-2026
entries.summary: Brand safety updates for product monographs have been released.
entries.why_it_matters: RA teams should review updated brand safety information for submissions cleared during September 2026.

entries.label: Health Canada
entries.title: Guide to reporting and providing information on drug shortages and discontinuations (GUI-0120)
entries.description: This document is intended to help market authorization holders comply with sections C.01.014.8 to C.01.014.91 of the Food and Drug Regulations
entries.summary: Provides guidance on reporting drug shortages and discontinuations to comply with sections C.01.014.8 to C.01.014.91 of the Food and Drug Regulations.
entries.why_it_matters: RA teams must include drug shortage information in regulatory submissions and communicate with authorities as required.

entries.label: Health Canada
entries.title: Guide to distributing drugs intended for the Canadian market for consumption or use outside Canada (GUI-0145)
entries.description: This document is intended to help drug establishment licence holders comply with sections C.01.014.94 to C.01.014.95 of the Food and Drug Regulations.
entries.summary: The guide provides instructions on how drug establishment licence holders can comply with sections C.01.014.94 to C.01.014.95 of the Food and Drug Regulations for distributing drugs intended for the Canadian market but used outside Canada.
entries.why_it_matters: Regulatory affairs teams responsible for international distribution must understand these compliance requirements to avoid regulatory breaches when exporting Canadian‑market drugs to other countries.

entries.label: Health Canada
entries.title: Guide on the exceptional importation and sale of drugs in response to shortages and discontinuations (GUI-0148)
entries.description: This document will help drug establishment licence holders comply with sections C.10.004 to C.10.013 of the Food and Drug Regulations.
entries.summary: The update provides a guideline on how to import and sell drugs during shortages and discontinuations to comply with sections C.10.004 to C.10.013 of the Food and Drug Regulations.
entries.why_it_matters: Regulatory affairs teams must review and apply this guideline to ensure their establishments meet the legal requirements for exceptional drug importation and sale during shortages or discontinuations.

entries.label: Health Canada
entries.title: Guide on extending expiration dates of marketed drugs in response to drug shortages (GUI-0500)
entries.description: This document will help market authorization holders and drug establishment licence holders understand how to comply with sections C.010.014 to C.10.021 of the Food and Drug Regulations
entries.summary: Provides guidance for extending expiration dates of marketed drugs to address shortages.
entries.why_it_matters: RA teams must review and potentially adjust expiry dates for affected products to remain compliant during shortages.

entries.label: Health Canada
entries.title: Register of Innovative Drugs
entries.description: A listing of drugs pursuant to sub-section C.08.004.1(9) of the Food and Drug Regulations.
entries.summary: A new register of innovative drugs has been established under sub-section C.08.004.1(9) of the Food and Drug Regulations.
entries.why_it_matters: RA teams handling innovative drug submissions must reference the register to ensure compliance with the updated regulatory framework.

entries.title: Drug Product Database data extract [2026-10-05]

entries.summary: The DPD data extract now includes complete information for all approved, marketed, and cancelled products across all product categories.
entries.why_it_matters: Regulatory affairs teams should use the updated extract to verify product status and ensure accurate documentation across human, veterinary, disinfectant, and radiopharmaceutical products.

entries.why_it_matters: RA teams must ensure type IA annual updates, individual type IA and type IAIN variations, and super‑groupings are submitted on time to obtain a 2026 outcome.

entries.title: Global regulators call for advancing alternatives to animal testing across the medicine lifecycle

entries.title: Member states contact points for review of national implementation of quick response (QR) codes of veterinary medicinal products authorised via the centralised (CP), mutual recognition (MRP), decentralised procedures (DCP) and national procedures

entries.why_it_matters: RA teams handling veterinary medicinal products must ensure compliance with the new QR code implementation and coordinate with the designated national contact points.

entries.why_it_matters: RA teams involved in clinical trials must be aware of the updated process to ensure timely cooperation and compliance with CHMP‑requested inspections.

entries.title: Monthly update to the generic submissions under review list

entries.why_it_matters: RA teams should be aware of the current submissions being reviewed to manage timelines and resource allocation.

entries.label: EMA Guidelines
entries.title: Substances considered as not falling within the scope of Regulation (EC) No. 470/2009, with regard to residues of veterinary medicinal products in foodstuffs of animal origin

entries.summary: Certain substances are now excluded from the scope of Regulation (EC) No. 470/2009 concerning residues of veterinary medicinal products in animal foodstuffs.
entries.why_it_matters: Veterinary regulatory teams must recognize that these excluded substances no longer require residue monitoring under the regulation, impacting compliance and testing strategies.

entries.title: Compliance and enforcement policy for health products (POL-0001)
entries.description: This policy describes Health Canada's national compliance and enforcement approach for health products regulated under the Food and Drugs Act and its regulations.
